findings.title: jsonwebtoken 10 inside stack-auth rejects or mishandles service-issued tokens, breaking auth for every encrypt/decrypt
findings.label: unsupported
findings.note: The cited lockfile and build_strategy lines show only that stack-auth uses jsonwebtoken, not that 0.42.2 handles tokens differently, so the auth-failure mechanism is speculative.

findings.title: jsonwebtoken 10's aws-lc-rs backend breaks the wasm32 build or panics at first token use on wasm
findings.label: valid
findings.note: Head Cargo.lock shows jsonwebtoken switching from ring to aws-lc-rs, and Cargo.toml/client_options.rs confirm stack-auth is compiled and used on wasm32, so a wasm build or runtime-provider failure is plausible and caused by the change; cargo tree with the wasm32 target is a concrete check.

findings.title: Rust crates move to 0.42.2 while the documented-lockstep npm @cipherstash/auth catalog stays at 0.42.0
findings.label: valid
findings.note: The cited dependabot.yml comment (=0.42.0, bump in step with the npm catalog) and the pnpm-workspace.yaml @cipherstash/auth 0.42.0 entry were left unchanged while the crates moved to 0.42.2, a real skew against documented policy that this change introduced.
